newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish insurer Warta Vita seeks foreign investor.
newsitem.headline: Polish insurer Warta Vita seeks foreign investor.

text.p: Shareholders of Polish life insurance company Warta Vita SA have agreed to offer a stake of up to 35.5 percent in the company to a foreign life insurance firm, a senior company official said on Thursday.

Stanislaw Puchala, the head of the firm's legal and administration department, told Reuters Warta Vita planned to boost its share capital to about 17 million zlotys from 11 million by issuing up to 600,000 new shares, that could be taken up by one or several foreign investors.

"It's an issue for a foreign investor, a life insurance company or companies...we have been negotiating with several of them and the shares could be offered between mid-December and mid-March," he said.
He added the firm was in talks with life insurance companies in France, Great Britain, Netherlands and Finland on selling the stake.
Warta Vita, which started operating in September last year, collected 2.9 million zlotys in gross premiums in the first nine months of 1996.

The current main Warta Vita shareholders are insurance company Warta, state-owned bank PKO BP, each holding 36.8-percent stakes, and Elektrim industrial and trading conglomerate which has 11.9 percent.
